ideas.title: USPSTF widens lung cancer screening: who newly qualifies, and why most eligible people still never get scanned
ideas.angle: Use the guideline change as the peg for a service-plus-tension story: who now qualifies (the age, pack-year and quit-date thresholds), whether insurers must cover it, and why low-dose CT uptake has stayed low even after the last expansion.
ideas.why_now: A fresh federal guideline change with direct personal-eligibility stakes, and insurance-coverage consequences that follow USPSTF grades.
ideas.is_it_real: Unverified and needs checking first. There is no source URL and the fact check is unverifiable. USPSTF last finalized lung screening in 2021. Confirm this is a new USPSTF draft or final recommendation, and not the American Cancer Society's 2023 guideline or another body's update being re-reported. Confirm the exact new thresholds before pitching.

notes: A light day: four newsroom-only terms, none with source URLs, and every fact check unverifiable. All four are therefore low confidence and conditional on finding primary sources. Two of them (H5N5 and sleep/dementia) are follow-ups attached to existing roundup items rather than new ideas. The lung screening item is the only one with pitch potential, but it hinges on confirming that USPSTF, not ACS or another body, actually changed its guidance.
